key_takeaways: Each overseas contract sets its own deposit, interim payments and balance dates, so check how much is due, by when and by what method before you sign.
With an invoice in the vendor's currency, the Australian dollar cost can move between deposit and balance, so hold a currency buffer as its own budget line.
Moneysmart suggests comparing exchange rates, fees and transfer times before you send money overseas, and notes a card international transaction fee may apply even to a payment in Australian dollars.
The ACCC advises calling a business on a number you have found yourself to confirm the payment details before you pay an emailed invoice.
Keep every contract, invoice, transfer confirmation and cash receipt together, and check your insurance once the first deposit is paid.

faq.q: How do you pay wedding vendors in another country?
faq.a: Follow each contract's payment schedule and method. Before each payment, compare the exchange rate, fees and transfer time, confirm the vendor's bank details by phone on a number you found yourself, and keep proof of every payment with the contract.

faq.q: Should I pay my overseas wedding vendors in AUD or their currency?
faq.a: With an invoice in the vendor's currency, the amount in that currency is fixed and your Australian dollar cost moves with the rate until you pay. A quote in Australian dollars still involves a conversion, so ask which rate it uses and whether it is fixed.

faq.q: How much deposit do overseas wedding vendors ask for?
faq.a: It varies, and each contract sets its own amount and dates. Before you sign, find the deposit, any interim payments, the balance date, the payment method and the point at which each payment stops being refundable.

faq.q: Is it safe to pay a wedding vendor overseas by bank transfer?
faq.a: It can be, if you confirm the details first. The ACCC urges Australians to check payment details directly with a business before paying an emailed invoice, by calling a number you have found yourself.

faq.q: What if my vendor abroad wants to be paid in cash?
faq.a: Treat it like any other payment term, with the amount, currency, date and recipient written into the contract. Ask for a written receipt for every cash payment, have one trusted person hand it over, and keep the receipts with your contracts.
